item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is the safer patch to review because it stays focused on the new convenience API. It still needs revision—most importantly, Upload must delegate to FilesService.Add—but A additionally changes request-body handling across the entire SDK, contrary to the frozen scope and behavior requirements.","reasons":["Both implementations violate the explicit requirement to route the multipart body through FilesService.Add; each duplicates Add's option processing, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error handling.","A modifies RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every io.Reader unless WithNoRetry is set. This changes Add, Update, and unrelated reader-backed requests globally, despite the contract explicitly forbidding unrelated retry refactoring and requiring existing Add behavior to remain unchanged.","A's buffering decision does not check whether the configured policy or HTTP method can actually retry, so it may eagerly consume and retain large streams even when no retry will occur.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and limits production changes to FilesService.Upload, making the necessary correction to delegate to Add small and reviewable rather than requiring removal of broad transport changes and associated documentation claims from A's patch excerpts shown here (raw.go, README.md, and CHANGELOG.md). A has materially stronger tests, but that advantage does not outweigh its production scope violation."],"risks_a":["Global eager buffering changes memory use, streaming behavior, and the timing of reader errors for all io.Reader request bodies.","FilesService.Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, creating duplicate request and error-handling machinery.","The changelog promises new retry behavior for Add and Update that the frozen contract specifically does not authorize."],"risks_b":["FilesService.Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and therefore does not preserve a single implementation point for options, requests, decoding, and errors.","The Upload test verifies the multipart field and filename but never reads and checks the uploaded content.","There are no Upload tests for retries, empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures, despite those being explicitly required."]}
